rationale: CanvasWidget's replay now tracks the sticky Canvas2D drawing state it applies (fill and stroke colour and paint server, line width/cap/join/miter/dash, font, text align, global alpha, blend mode, shadow, filter, direction, image smoothing) and, after each recorded restore, re-applies every slot that differs from the matching save, so restore() reverts the drawing state identically on Skia and CoreGraphics. The retained-ui-kernel touch is confined to canvas_widget.cpp's replay loop: the sticky-state setter cases move into the new canvas_replay_state.cpp helper and the save/restore/draw-image-placeholder cases call it. This is what lets Pulp's own web-compat Canvas2D shim keep its record of sent state across save/restore, which is Pulp's JS bridge wire with no counterpart framework behaviour to backport, so it is recorded pulp-only.
